scenarios.name: cooling_loop_modulating_on_setpoint
scenarios.description: Ordinary zone cooling: the discharge sits on its 13 °C setpoint with the chilled-water valve at 55%. The loop has reserve in both directions, which is what a healthy fan coil looks like, and yClgFullOk is false because a loop that has not saturated is one this rule has no verdict about

scenarios.name: valve_wide_open_holding_setpoint
scenarios.description: The valve is at 100% and the discharge is 0.5 °C high — a coil sized close to its design point on a design day. Half a degree is inside ε_sat, so this is a unit at capacity rather than a unit that has lost capacity, and here the silence is a health claim: yClgFullOk is true

scenarios.name: sat_error_just_below_threshold
scenarios.description: One tenth inside the allowance: sat − sat_sp = 0.9 °C at a saturated valve. Silent, and the closest healthy case to the boundary

scenarios.name: sat_error_exactly_at_threshold
scenarios.description: Threshold edge: sat − sat_sp = 1.0 °C exactly, the whole ε_sat allowance, with the valve at 100%. `spMiss` is a strict `>`, so an error sitting precisely on the sensor allowance reads healthy

scenarios.name: sat_error_just_over_threshold
scenarios.description: Threshold edge, other side: 1.1 °C above setpoint at a 100% valve clears the strict comparison on the first tick, and with delayOnInit the alarm asserts at exactly one alarm_delay (1800 s)

scenarios.name: valve_just_below_full_threshold
scenarios.description: Command edge: a 5 °C setpoint miss with the valve at 98.9%. Below cc_full_threshold the loop still has something to ask for, so yClgFullOk is false and this rule has no verdict — the miss is real and belongs to a loop-response rule, not to this one

scenarios.name: valve_exactly_at_full_threshold
scenarios.description: Command edge: the same 5 °C miss with the valve parked on exactly 99.0%. `clgFull` is a strict `>`, so a command sitting on cc_full_threshold does not count as saturated and the rule stays silent where the reference's `≥ 99%` would report

scenarios.name: valve_just_over_full_threshold
scenarios.description: Command edge, third side: the same 5 °C miss at 99.5% clears the strict comparison, yClgFullOk goes true, and the alarm lands after alarm_delay

scenarios.name: coil_saturated_and_missing_setpoint
scenarios.description: The motivating case: the valve is wide open and the discharge is stuck 5 °C above setpoint. The loop has asked for everything it has and the air has not moved — chilled water too warm, a fouled coil, a valve that reports open and is not, or a stalled fan leaving stagnant room air on the sensor

scenarios.name: miss_opens_mid_run
scenarios.description: A rising edge mid-run rather than at load: the unit holds setpoint at a saturated valve until the chilled-water riser warms at t = 600 s, after which the discharge sits 5 °C high. The alarm lands at exactly 600 + 1800 = 2400 s

scenarios.name: morning_pulldown_clears_before_delay
scenarios.description: Transient: the valve pins at 100% and the discharge runs 5 °C high while the coil pulls a hotel room down after an unoccupied night, reaching setpoint at t = 1200 s. A pulldown is shorter than alarm_delay, so nothing alarms

scenarios.name: fault_clears_when_chilled_water_returns
scenarios.description: A saturated valve missing setpoint alarms at 1800 s; the riser comes back at t = 3000 s and the discharge reaches setpoint. `TrueDelay` has no off-delay, so the alarm drops on that tick

scenarios.name: valve_backs_off_before_delay
scenarios.description: Recovery through the command term: the discharge stays 5 °C high but the valve modulates back to 80% at t = 1200 s. yClgFullOk goes false, persistence restarts, and no alarm follows — a loop with reserve left is a loop still working, and the saturation half is what makes the setpoint miss evidence of a defect

scenarios.name: setpoint_reset_upward_clears_the_miss
scenarios.description: The setpoint moves, not the air: the discharge holds 18 °C at a saturated valve while the sequence resets sat_sp from 13 °C to 17.5 °C at t = 1200 s. The remaining 0.5 °C gap is inside ε_sat, so the rule falls silent — the comparison is against the active setpoint, which is why the preconditions insist on the one the sequence is actually holding

scenarios.name: hunting_loop_never_alarms
scenarios.description: A hunting cooling loop swings the discharge between 18 °C and 12.8 °C on a 20-minute period with the valve pinned open. Its mean sits well above setpoint and a 5-minute rolling average would report the fault, but persistence restarts on every compliant tick, so this rule stays silent — the limit of substituting TrueDelay for averaging (see Deviations)
